bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to state government; prohibiting legislators and executive branch appointees from receiving compensation from any nonprofit organization that receives state grant funding; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 3.084, subdivision 2; 15.0597, by adding a subdivision; 15.06, subdivision 9.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 3.084, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
Prohibition.
(a) A sitting member of the legislature is prohibited from accepting employment with or otherwise receiving compensation for services performed from:
(1) a business whose primary source of revenue is derived from lobbying, government relations or government affairs services;
(2) a business whose primary source of revenue is derived from facilitating government relations or government affairs services between two third parties; [-or -]
(3) any other business that employs or contracts with lobbyists, government relations or government affairs professionals, if the member's job duties include acting in that capacity or providing direct or indirect consulting, advice, or administrative support for that work[+; or +]
[+(4) a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state+].
(b) This prohibition applies regardless of the location where the work of the business is substantially conducted or its clients are located.
(c) The house of representatives and the senate must adopt rules to enforce this section.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 15.0597, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 9.+]

[+Private employment and compensation.+]

[+At the time of appointment and while serving as an appointed member of a multimember agency, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state. +]

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 15.06, subdivision 9, is amended to read:

Subd. 9.
Private employment[+ and compensation+].
[+(a) +]No former commissioner or deputy commissioner may, within one year after leaving the position of commissioner or deputy commissioner in a department or agency, appear or participate in proceedings of that department or agency representing the interests of private persons.

[+(b) At the time of appointment and while serving as a commissioner or deputy commissioner, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to state government; prohibiting legislators and executive branch appointees from receiving compensation from any nonprofit organization that receives state grant funding; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 3.084, subdivision 2; 15.0597, by adding a subdivision; 15.06, subdivision 9.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 3.084, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
Prohibition.
(a) A sitting member of the legislature is prohibited from accepting employment with or otherwise receiving compensation for services performed from:
(1) a business whose primary source of revenue is derived from lobbying, government relations or government affairs services;
(2) a business whose primary source of revenue is derived from facilitating government relations or government affairs services between two third parties;
(3) any other business that employs or contracts with lobbyists, government relations or government affairs professionals, if the member's job duties include acting in that capacity or providing direct or indirect consulting, advice, or administrative support for that work; or
(4) a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state.
(b) This prohibition applies regardless of the location where the work of the business is substantially conducted or its clients are located.
(c) The house of representatives and the senate must adopt rules to enforce this section.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 15.0597, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 9.

Private employment and compensation.

At the time of appointment and while serving as an appointed member of a multimember agency, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 15.06, subdivision 9, is amended to read:

Subd. 9.
Private employment and compensation.
(a) No former commissioner or deputy commissioner may, within one year after leaving the position of commissioner or deputy commissioner in a department or agency, appear or participate in proceedings of that department or agency representing the interests of private persons.

(b) At the time of appointment and while serving as a commissioner or deputy commissioner, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state.
additions: (4) a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state

At the time of appointment and while serving as an appointed member of a multimember agency, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state.

(b) At the time of appointment and while serving as a commissioner or deputy commissioner, a person must not be employed by or otherwise receive compensation for services performed from a nonprofit organization that receives grant funding from the state.
